newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed with the falling domestic A share markets unable to support the contracts despite their current low rates, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded three-day contract fell sharply to 2.90 percent from 6.70 percent on Thursday.
Traders said the three-day contract fell because institutions did not borrow as much short-term money as usual with the weekend approaching.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 3.57 million lots from 7.4 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the weak performance of the domestic A share markets prevented big institutions from entering the market.
The A market's performance will continue to be a key factor next week, they said.
"The rates are likely to move in a narrow range next week because there are only a few A share issues," one trader said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed on Friday after the most active 10-year bond with a maturity date of in June 2006 met resistance in intra-day trading, traders said.
The 10-year bond fell to 118.80 yuan from 118.95 yuan after failing to breach the 119-yuan resistance level, traders said.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell to 1.4 million lots from 1.6 million lots.
Traders said that market sentiment was good with money supply increasing as a result of substantial redemption of state debt recently, and that the contracts were likely to rise next week.
